scenes.headline: How scaling laws decide where a budget goes
scenes.sub: Kaplan, Chinchilla, and the two results that added a third axis.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Tapioca! Everyone quotes twenty tokens per parameter. Models shipping now run thousands of times past it. Here's why both are right.

scenes.text: Loss falls predictably as you spend. The best split of the spend depends on which costs you count: training, serving, or inference samples.
scenes.say: Loss falls predictably as you spend. But the best way to split the spend depends on which costs you count: training, serving, or inference samples.

scenes.title: The line, and why it is shallow
scenes.say: Kaplan and colleagues found loss falls as a power law in parameters, data and compute.

parts.note: how low the loss floor sits once training ends
parts.say: It doesn't describe the walk downhill. It predicts how low the floor sits once training ends.

parts.note: compute spent, against a fitted constant
parts.say: On log axes it's a straight line, across more than seven orders of magnitude. That makes big runs a planning exercise.

parts.note: 10x the compute removes about 11% of the remaining loss
parts.say: But the exponent is tiny. Ten times the compute removes only about eleven percent of the remaining loss.

scenes.title: Four answers to one allocation question
scenes.say: The line held. What changed is which costs go into the budget.

items.say: Kaplan's reading: for a training budget, spend on parameters.

items.text: Chinchilla: grow parameters and tokens together
items.say: Chinchilla trained over four hundred models and found both should grow together: about twenty tokens per parameter.

items.text: Sardana: put serving in the cost
items.say: But serving is paid per parameter. Put it in the objective, and the optimum moves to a hundred to two hundred.
Add the samples drawn at inference, and it shifts further, well into over-training a smaller model.

scenes.title: Tokens per parameter
scenes.say: So models shipping now run at two hundred and fourteen tokens per parameter, at sixty thousand, even seventy-nine thousand. That isn't drift. It's a different objective.

scenes.text: A scaling law is a conditional statement: before quoting a ratio, ask which budget it was optimising.

recap: Loss falls on a straight, shallow line
Serving and sampling push toward over-training
scenes.say: To recap: a straight but shallow line, twenty to one for training alone, and over-training once serving and sampling count.
